adventure.title: Hill Repeats on the Exorcist Steps
adventure.description: The seventy-five stone steps from M Street up to Prospect — made famous by the movie — double as Georgetown's most brutal free workout, with rowers on the Potomac below as your recovery view.
adventure.bonus: Five rounds minimum — and walk down backwards once, just to say you did.

adventure.title: Skate the Sculpture Garden Ice Rink
adventure.description: Every winter the National Gallery's Sculpture Garden fountain freezes into DC's most elegant ice rink — laps under the Calder and Lichtenstein with hot chocolate waiting at the Pavilion Café.
adventure.bonus: Skate until the lights come on — the sculptures change completely after dark.

adventure.title: Monuments by Moonlight Paddle — Key Bridge Boathouse
adventure.description: Key Bridge Boathouse's guided evening paddle puts you on the Potomac with the lit Lincoln and the Kennedy Center reflected across open water — the monuments the way almost nobody sees them.
adventure.bonus: Stop paddling mid-river, close your eyes for 30 seconds, then open them — no explanation, just do it.

adventure.title: Gravelly Point Plane Spotting Picnic
adventure.description: Planes from Reagan National clear fifty feet overhead while you sprawl on the grass at Gravelly Point, making it the most exhilarating free picnic spot on the East Coast.
adventure.bonus: Track an inbound flight on FlightAware and count down its approach — stand and wave as it thunders over.

adventure.title: Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens at Dawn
adventure.description: DC's only national park dedicated to water plants erupts with blooming lotus and lily pads each summer morning before the heat closes the flowers by noon.
adventure.bonus: Get a photo of a lotus bloom fully open — you have until 10 AM before they start closing.

adventure.title: Anacostia Riverwalk Trail to Frederick Douglass House
adventure.description: The paved Anacostia Riverwalk delivers a rarely-walked slice of DC history, ending at Cedar Hill where Frederick Douglass's views of the Capitol are genuinely humbling.
adventure.bonus: Stand on Douglass's front porch and recite a single line from one of his speeches out loud.

adventure.title: National Mall Dawn Run — Monument Circuit
adventure.description: The 4.5-mile loop past the Lincoln, Vietnam, Korea, FDR, MLK, and Jefferson memorials at dawn — the monuments at first light with no crowds is the best DC has to offer.
adventure.bonus: Stop at each memorial and read one inscription out loud.

adventure.title: Great Falls Maryland — Billy Goat Trail A
adventure.description: The Class A section of the Billy Goat Trail scrambles along the Mather Gorge above the Potomac falls — more technical than a hike, views that explain why people move to DC.
adventure.bonus: Find the point where the gorge is narrowest and listen to the water for two minutes.

adventure.title: Capital One Arena — Caps or Wizards Night
adventure.description: The F Street corridor before a game is DC's best sports energy — the arena is intimate, the city gets loud, and the pregame bar scene on 7th St NW is mandatory.
adventure.bonus: Make friends with someone in your section by the second period.

adventure.title: National Museum of African American History
adventure.description: Book timed-entry passes months in advance — the Smithsonian's bronze lattice-wrapped building on the Mall is the most important museum in DC and requires a full day.
adventure.bonus: Start in the basement and work your way up chronologically — don't skip a floor.

adventure.title: Eastern Market Flea + Neighborhood Loop
adventure.description: Start at the weekend flea market outside Eastern Market, walk the Capitol Hill rowhouse blocks east, grab a Blue Bench crepe inside, and loop back through Lincoln Park.
adventure.bonus: Buy one thing from the flea market you had no intention of buying.

adventure.title: Capital Crescent Trail — Georgetown to Silver Spring
adventure.description: 11 miles of paved trail through Georgetown, Bethesda, and Silver Spring on the old B&O Railroad bed — flat, shaded, and the best bike commute in the metro area.
adventure.bonus: Ride the full 11 miles without stopping — time yourself each direction.

adventure.title: Mount Vernon by Boat from The Wharf
adventure.description: Take the Spirit of Mount Vernon from Pier 4 at The Wharf — three hours on the Potomac, tour Washington's estate, sail back as the sun drops behind Virginia.
adventure.bonus: Find the distillery on the estate grounds — it's operational and selling whiskey.

adventure.title: Potomac River Kayak from Thompson Boat
adventure.description: Rent a kayak from Thompson Boat Center under the Key Bridge and paddle downriver past Georgetown's waterfront, under the bridges, past the Kennedy Center.
adventure.bonus: Paddle under all three Georgetown bridges without stopping.

adventure.title: Mount Vernon Trail Run — Key Bridge South
adventure.description: Cross Key Bridge into Virginia and run south on the Mount Vernon Trail along the Potomac — airport views, Pentagon backdrop, 18 miles total if you push it.
adventure.bonus: Run to the Reagan National Airport overlook and watch a plane land 200 feet overhead.

adventure.title: Tidal Basin Paddleboat
adventure.description: Rent a paddleboat from the Tidal Basin Boathouse and pedal around the basin with the Jefferson Memorial dead ahead and the Washington Monument reflected in the water.
adventure.bonus: Get close enough to the Jefferson Memorial to read the inscription above the columns.

adventure.title: International Spy Museum Deep Dive
adventure.description: The L'Enfant Plaza museum is genuinely excellent — actual tradecraft artifacts, real declassified ops, and an interactive cover assignment that runs through the whole visit.
adventure.bonus: Complete your cover assignment without breaking character once.

adventure.title: Library of Congress — Great Hall & Lantern
adventure.description: The Jefferson Building's Great Hall is one of the most ornate interiors in America — go to the Visitor Gallery to see the original Gutenberg Bible and book the lantern dome tour.
adventure.bonus: Book the lantern dome tour to get to the top of the Reading Room dome — it fills fast.

adventure.title: C&O Canal Towpath Bike — Georgetown to Great Falls
adventure.description: 14.3 miles of flat gravel towpath along the historic canal from Georgetown to the Great Falls overlook — no cars, no hills, pure DC history under your wheels.
adventure.bonus: Stop at every lockhouse you pass and read the historical marker.

adventure.title: Great Falls Park Hike, Virginia Side
adventure.description: The Potomac drops 76 feet over jagged rocks fifteen miles from the Capitol — the overlooks on the Virginia side put you close enough to feel the spray in high water.
adventure.bonus: Hike down to the river's edge at Overlook 3 when water is high — get close enough that you can't hear the person next to you speak.

adventure.title: Climb at Movement Crystal City
adventure.description: Movement Crystal City — opened by Earth Treks as the largest climbing gym in the country — runs walls up to 50 feet with routes that humble anyone.
adventure.bonus: Attempt the hardest bouldering problem rated on the board — one legitimate try, no beta from YouTube.

adventure.title: Rock Creek Park Trail Run
adventure.description: 1,700 acres of forested trails running through the middle of the city — the Western Ridge and Valley trails feel genuinely remote for a place ten minutes from downtown.
adventure.bonus: Find Pulpit Rock — the actual boulder — and climb it. Post nothing about it.

adventure.title: Night Monuments Tour by Bike — Capital Bikeshare
adventure.description: Every major monument is lit and almost empty after 10pm, and looping the Mall on a bikeshare at night is the closest DC gets to cinematic.
adventure.bonus: Hit all five: Lincoln, Vietnam Wall, Korean War, FDR, and Jefferson memorials in one unbroken loop without stopping the clock — under 90 minutes.

adventure.title: Sunrise at the Lincoln Memorial Steps
adventure.description: The Mall is deserted at dawn and the reflection pool turns the monument into something genuinely monumental — no crowds, no noise, just marble and light.
adventure.bonus: Sit exactly where MLK stood during the 'I Have a Dream' speech — the engraved marker is there. Read the full Gettysburg Address carved inside out loud.

social.title: Show Night at Black Cat, 14th Street
social.description: DC's indie rock institution has anchored 14th Street since 1993 — two stages, a red room bar with pinball, and a booking policy that still takes chances on weird.
social.bonus: Buy the opener's merch if they win you over — tell them which song did it.

social.title: Sunday Afternoon at Bardo Brewpub, Ivy City
social.description: Bardo's sprawling outdoor beer garden in Ivy City is the city's most comfortable Sunday sprawl — giant pours, food trucks, and a crowd that's entirely in on the secret.
social.bonus: Challenge a stranger to a round of cornhole — loser buys the next round.

social.title: Drink at Off the Record, Hay-Adams Hotel
social.description: The subterranean bar beneath the Hay-Adams is packed with caricatures of political figures and actual political figures, and the martinis are cold enough to make you brave.
social.bonus: Identify three caricatures on the wall without using your phone — ask the bartender to settle any disputes.

social.title: 9:30 Club Show on V Street
social.description: Consistently voted the best live music venue in DC — standing room, great sightlines, the best sound system in a club this size, and a calendar that never disappoints.
social.bonus: Get as close to the stage as possible and stay there the whole show.

social.title: JFK's Booth at Martin's Tavern
social.description: The Georgetown pub where JFK proposed to Jackie in 1953 — sit in Booth #3, order a Guinness, and appreciate that some places earn their mythology.
social.bonus: Ask the bartender which other historical figures claimed a regular booth.

social.title: Kramers Late Night, Dupont
social.description: The only bookstore-cafe in DC open 24 hours on weekends — browse the shelves at midnight, order a glass of wine at the cafe, stay as long as you want.
social.bonus: Buy one book you'd never pick in daylight and read the first chapter there.

social.title: Dacha Beer Garden, Shaw
social.description: The Shaw outdoor beer garden with long communal tables, a rotating tap list, and the kind of warm-weather Saturday energy that makes DC feel like it got out of its own way.
social.bonus: Introduce yourself to whoever is sharing your table — that's the point.

social.title: Blues Alley Jazz Supper Club
social.description: The legendary Georgetown jazz club in the alley off Wisconsin Ave has hosted every name worth knowing — dinner at a table, a show that goes until midnight.
social.bonus: Go without looking up who's playing — let the night surprise you.

social.title: Late Night at The Hamilton Live
social.description: The Hamilton is a massive subterranean music venue under a restaurant two blocks from the White House — the late sets run past midnight and the room sounds incredible.
social.bonus: Get to the front third of the standing area before the headliner — and introduce yourself to whoever ends up next to you.

social.title: Bar Night at Round Robin Bar, Willard Hotel
social.description: The circular bar inside the Willard InterContinental has been mixing drinks for senators and presidents since 1850 — order the Mint Julep and let the room do the work.
social.bonus: Ask the bartender to name the most historically significant person who ever sat at your exact stool — then order whatever that person supposedly drank.

foodie.title: Soul Food Counter at Oohh's & Aahh's, U Street
foodie.description: This unassuming U Street counter has heaped plates with catfish, candied yams, and the city's best mac and cheese for over two decades — sit down and order whatever the person next to you is having.
foodie.bonus: Ask the cashier what they ate for lunch today — then order that.

foodie.title: Old Ebbitt Grill Oyster Bar
foodie.description: DC's oldest saloon, two blocks from the White House — sit at the curved mahogany bar, order two dozen raw oysters, and a very cold martini.
foodie.bonus: Ask the shucker which oyster they'd eat twice — then order six of those.

foodie.title: Half Smoke at Ben's Next Door
foodie.description: The bar next door to the institution on U Street — same half smoke, cold beer, late hours, and a little more room to breathe than the original.
foodie.bonus: Order the chili cheese fries alongside the half smoke and don't share them.

foodie.title: Call Your Mother Bagels, Capitol Hill
foodie.description: The Capitol Hill bagel shop that became a DC institution — get the everything with smash smear and lox, eat it on the steps outside like everyone else does.
foodie.bonus: Order the most complicated bagel on the menu and eat it in under five minutes.

foodie.title: Ambar Unlimited Tasting, Capitol Hill
foodie.description: Balkan small plates on the Hill with an unlimited tasting menu that keeps coming until you stop asking — the rakija, the cevapi, the burek are all essential.
foodie.bonus: Order at least one dish you've never heard of and can't pronounce.

foodie.title: Founding Farmers Weekend Brunch
foodie.description: The farm-to-table anchor near the World Bank does a full weekend brunch spread with bottomless mimosas and the kind of pancakes that end the debate.
foodie.bonus: Get there at opening — the line by 10am is real.

foodie.title: Rose's Luxury, Capitol Hill
foodie.description: James Beard Award winner, no reservations — get there when the door opens, put your name in, drink somewhere nearby, and come back for the best dinner in DC.
foodie.bonus: Order the lychee and habanero salad even if it sounds wrong — it's not.

foodie.title: Joe's Seafood Stone Crab Claws
foodie.description: The DC outpost of the Miami stone crab institution — order the large claws in season (Oct–May) with the mustard sauce and nothing else.
foodie.bonus: Crack every claw yourself — no help, no tools, just the mallet.

foodie.title: Eastern Market Saturday Morning Feed
foodie.description: The South Hall vendors at Eastern Market have been feeding Capitol Hill since 1873 — grab a blueberry buckwheat pancake from Market Lunch and eat it on the outdoor steps.
foodie.bonus: Join the Market Lunch line before 8am and talk to the person behind you — ask them what they're ordering and match it exactly.

foodie.title: Dinner at Minibar by José Andrés
foodie.description: Twenty-plus courses in a six-seat counter restaurant from the chef who invented DC's fine dining scene — this is the most technically ambitious meal in the city, full stop.
foodie.bonus: Ask the chef staffing your counter to explain the most technically difficult dish of the night — and actually push them on the chemistry.

foodie.title: Dim Sum Brunch at China Garden, Rockville Pike
foodie.description: The cart-service dim sum at this massive Rockville institution draws the entire regional Chinese community on weekends — the har gow alone justifies the drive.
foodie.bonus: Order entirely by pointing — no English menu — and eat whatever arrives without asking what it is first.

foodie.title: Lunch at Ben's Chili Bowl, U Street
foodie.description: A half-smoke with mustard and chili at the counter of DC's most legendary diner — open since 1958 — is the one meal that explains this city's soul.
foodie.bonus: Order at the counter, sit on a stool, and strike up a conversation with whoever's next to you — then ask them the best thing they've eaten in DC this week.

chill.title: Tidal Basin at Cherry Blossom Peak
chill.description: Peak bloom around the Tidal Basin lasts exactly four to five days — go at 6am before the crowds arrive and the Jefferson Memorial and Washington Monument are framed in pink.
chill.bonus: Come back at dusk on the same day — the light is completely different.

chill.title: Georgetown C&O Canal Towpath Evening
chill.description: The flat canal towpath through Georgetown at golden hour — quiet, no cars, mule-drawn boat history in every lockhouse, and the Potomac visible through the trees.
chill.bonus: Walk until you reach Lock 3 and back without looking at your phone.

chill.title: National Arboretum — Bonsai & Capitol Columns
chill.description: The free 446-acre botanical garden in NE DC has the national bonsai collection, the original Capitol columns reassembled on a hill, and zero tourists on a weekday.
chill.bonus: Find the oldest bonsai in the collection and read its history card.

chill.title: Hillwood Estate & Japanese Garden
chill.description: Marjorie Merriweather Post's Rock Creek Park mansion with the finest collection of Russian Imperial art outside Russia and a Japanese garden that has no business being this good.
chill.bonus: Find one object in the mansion that costs more than your car.

chill.title: Theodore Roosevelt Island Trail
chill.description: The 88-acre wilderness island in the middle of the Potomac accessible only by footbridge from Rosslyn — 2.5 miles of trail, a memorial plaza, almost no one knows it exists.
chill.bonus: Read one of the four TR quotes on the memorial wall and pick which one is best.

chill.title: Meridian Hill Park Sunday Drumming
chill.description: Every Sunday afternoon the cascading fountain park in Columbia Heights hosts a community drumming circle that's been going since the 1950s — bring nothing, just show up.
chill.bonus: Stay for the full two hours without checking your phone once.

chill.title: Coffee at Tryst, Adams Morgan
chill.description: Tryst has been the living room of Adams Morgan since 1999 — mismatched couches, strong coffee, and zero pressure to leave at any point.
chill.bonus: Leave your phone face-down for the entire visit and strike up a conversation with a stranger instead.

chill.title: Afternoon at Dumbarton Oaks Garden, Georgetown
chill.description: These ten acres of formal gardens hidden above Georgetown are the most quietly stunning outdoor space in DC — manicured for decades and almost always peaceful.
chill.bonus: Find the Pebble Garden — sit on the stone bench and stay completely silent for five full minutes.

culture.title: National Cathedral Tower at Sunset
culture.description: Take the elevator to the top of the Gloria in Excelsis Tower for a 360-degree view of the city — the Washington Monument to the south, Maryland to the north, at golden hour.
culture.bonus: Find the Darth Vader grotesque on the northwest tower before you leave.

culture.title: Nationals Park Half Smoke & Rooftop
culture.description: The Navy Yard ballpark has the Capitol dome over center field, Ben's Chili Bowl in the concourse, and a rooftop bar in right field — buy the cheap ticket and upgrade your view.
culture.bonus: Get the half smoke from the Ben's stand inside and eat it during the national anthem.

culture.title: National Portrait Gallery Free Night
culture.description: The Smithsonian American Art Museum and National Portrait Gallery share a building in Penn Quarter — free always, uncrowded on weeknights, the Lunder Conservation Center lets you watch art being restored.
culture.bonus: Find one portrait where you can't tell the subject is famous until you read the label.

culture.title: Free Friday Night at the Hirshhorn Museum
culture.description: The Hirshhorn's contemporary art collection is massive and completely free — Friday evenings thin the crowds and the cylindrical building alone is worth the visit.
culture.bonus: Find the most divisive piece in the current exhibition and defend it to whoever you're with — two minutes minimum.

culture.title: National Gallery of Art Sculpture Garden
culture.description: The fountain plaza is free, the modern sculptures are world-class, and on a clear afternoon it might be the most civilized outdoor hour available anywhere on the Mall.
culture.bonus: Pick the sculpture you find least interesting and stand in front of it for ten full minutes — then decide if you still feel the same.

culture.title: Reading Room at the Library of Congress
culture.description: The Main Reading Room of the Thomas Jefferson Building is one of the most beautiful interiors in America and anyone can walk in, look up, and feel humbled.
culture.bonus: Request an actual book from the stacks — any book — and read a full chapter under that dome.
